name: CT-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Joe Courtney has a large financial edge and no outside opposition
District leans Democratic and the national environment favors Democrats
Prediction markets price Courtney at about 97% to win
No public polling or expert ratings, so uncertainty is elevated
model.rationale: Courtney combines a Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and a roughly two-to-one fundraising advantage over George Austin, while markets price him near certain. With no polls available, the forecast rests on fundamentals, which point to a comfortable double-digit Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Austin closing within single digits, or significant outside spending against Courtney, would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Eastern Connecticut's 2nd District leans Democratic by about four points, and six-term incumbent Joe Courtney is seeking reelection with the advantages that entails. He has raised roughly $760,000 and holds about $600,000 on hand, while Republican George Austin has raised about $314,000 with modest cash reserves. No outside groups are opposing Courtney, and a small amount of outside spending supports him.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and market pricing. Prediction markets put Courtney's chances near 97 percent. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and the financial gap points to a solid Democratic win, though the absence of polling keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated.
